Andicators and all other painting tools . But now I believe that a blind man could see the light if and only if it is touched. After pass the following topics RBD,DBR CP SUPPLY AND DEMAND FTR,FTB,… I intend to continue my trading journey here . I will be starting what an ENGULF means. But first I would like to infrastructure to topic. Before we begin I would like to emphasize that I am a novice and this is just what I've seen in this two month. And at the end, I apologize for the lack of English language. The smallest member of this community Salivan First, I will address several questions. 1-What is the market? 2-Who will drive the market ? 3-What is their purpose? 4-Why RTM ? 5- What are our weapons ? 6-How a tool works? 7-Why it works? Now I try to answer these questions in my point of view . 1-What is the market ? I think the market is a jungle .there are the number of bull ,the bears, the dogs, the lambs and the pigs in this jungle that they fight to each other's. 2-who will drive the Market ? In my idea the dogs .they called them Big Boys , Smart Money , IT s . Dogs are loyal to their commitments. And I think all the things that one need in this jungle is loyalty to its commitments. So that They eventually wins. 3-what is their purpose ? What are their obligations ? They need to empty the pockets of others either bulls or bears . 4- why RTM ? For me , because RTM showed me in what areas ,the moderator of this jungle is waiting for it's prey to hunt them and it is not important if they are bear or bull or lamb or pigs. Here, kill or be killed. 5-What are our weapons ? There are a lot of armaments in this castle. SUPPLY & DEMAND,RBD,DBR,CP,ENGULF,FO,3DERIVE,QUASIMODO,CAN-CAN,FLAGS and some others. 6-How a tool works ? In the videos, Mr. IF has told us how a tool works and how we can use them, also the masters wrote some articles for us, that I call all this collection, the art of war . 7-why it works ? This is the most important part .because the I think it's more important why a tool work that what it works . So that I start with RBD,DBR s. What is RBD ,DBR ??? RALLY BASE DROP : Generally We call it supply . it's The resistance against rising prices.it Contains the worst buyers and also some decision points that sellers exceeds buyers . so that if any decision made there that price is too expensive we expect in future the big boys can grab some orders from unsuspecting traders or the worst buyers here again . so that this zone is full of DPs. I think all the market are DP s.in this case Some decisions have been taken to reduce the price . but why they think price is here too expensive ?? Psychologically, people tend to repeat their decisions in life the decisions that altered the course of prices in general are important to us. So that if the price is reduced with these decisions we call this area that the decision have been made in it, supply (RBD).and the same applies to regional demand(DBR).some decision have been taken that price is too cheap so the big boys can grab some orders from the novice traders like me in that area in future again.in this case some decision have been taken to rally the price and support it.so This set of decisions in that area, that the price is cheap cause a DBR for us that we call it DEMAND area . But the quality of development of these areas are important to us. How and in what form they are formed is very important. Do they have a firm decision or indecision has occurred in past ??these are also important . Another issue is approaching the prices to these areas.so that if price approaching to a fresh area as a compression we can expect that area to work again as before. But if price approaching the area Strictly we should wait and use other weapons . I think all the market is fear and greed. Those CPs represents the fear. And high volatility is indicate the greed . so that in greed we should pay more attention to other weapons why the opponent does not fear losing and very assertive in approaching our privacy. our privacy is our castle , where we already have seen fighters failure. If you look into the real world you will see that the losers always fear at The places where they have failed there . So this is a psychological reason. This forest is a mirror of the behavior of its residents. After a number of failed raid to break up the castle If they want to break the barrier must gather more power so they go down to reinvigoratewe, call it deep pullbacks. This is what we see in the real world. Castle also been hitting so that it's too weak for the next attack and we call this consumptions of the orders. Weakness or strength of the castle can be determined from something that we call it SUPPLY & DEMAND. I want to say that I see the difference between SUPPLY with RBD and DEMAND with DBR . I will explain the reason, In future. Therefore the more attacking to a castle cause it weaker and in the next raid, it may be rejected by the stronger amount of attackers. This how I read the story . After that we have some other weapons to determine whether a castle resistance against the attacks or not ? Something that called CP. Compression is a kind of fear. But sometimes this is fear that gives courage. My fear is what gives me the courage. Again, these two issues are related to underpin our castle .A new castle usually resistance against the fear of the attackers . Retreat or recess of warriors in the way up toapproaching the castle is a sign that they fear . After reaching the Castle The first warrior who fail ,break the morale of the fighters . On the other hand if the army on the way forward reach to a coward Front ,Of course, it will be faster to defeat it . now what is the difference between SUPPLY and RBD ? Imagine we want to build a fortress. a fortress which contains many castle that Each castle has a flag . in my idea even a strong fortress on a loose ground cannot withstand the attacks .so that I consider supply as a ground as the foundation of the fortress and consider the fortress as RBD. vice versa for DEMAND and DBR too. In the RBD the upper castle in this case the extreme edge of the fortress is SUPPLY area that resistance against the Attackers. The question that must be asked here is that Why this Classifications are important for me ? If attackers can infiltrate a castle after a while they vivify their power then march in the same direction of the seepage to approach another castle on their way . how much to be returning to shore power depends on the strength of the fortress collapsed, that RTM call it as ENGULF . I have another question: Who make this ENGULF ? No one in particular , The only things that make penetration occurs are the fort foundation strength and the strength of the invaders blows. The question is whether the big boy makes an engulf or all attackers make it? Or do engulf pre-made and big boy sees it and then decide for it ? This question also are right and logical . In my idea all these issues together, provides the ENGULF : A. The weakness of the land on which the castle was established on it . In this case SUPPLY & DEMAND (Combination of fortresses that collapsed earlier) B. Amount of fresh attackers and how long it takes to accumulating fresh power to continue their way . C. BIG BOYS (heroes) are also analysis the war and novices are do it too . I will try to prove and also improve this story .in the next part of this article I will try to anatomize the topic engulf . Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6699 THE ART OF WAR PART2 In the previous section PART 1 I tried to tell clip of a battle. A war in which fighters are trying to conquer the castles in the air. Decisions should be taken to conquer a castle. Places where decisions are taken are important for us. The think tanks! If you want to destroy a castle ,at first penetrate to the think tanks . Before conquering a castle it should be breached. We as a trader there is no matter if a fortress conquered by bulls or bears . We're just looking to make a profit in this war and wherever a permeation occurs we accompany the fighters. So we want to be loyal to our rules, not the rules of the war. In the meantime, there are signs to those who deal with THE RTM ART OF WAR. WHAT IS AN ENGULF ? The most important question in RTM training camp. First of all I want to describe a hypothetical battle. Suppose that an army is advancing to conquer the enemy positions. Enemy positions include a number of castles that formed a fortress. To conquer a fortress its FLAG should be conquer. As soon as the flag of first castle was removed we must ask ourselves a few questions. 1- What is the position of the conquered castle? 2- Where they come from and where are they now? 3- Is there a nearby castle, which is already under attack? 4- After the conquest of the castle and down the old flag, did the attackers have raised their flag? 5- Where is the nearest room to think and also where is next think tank that should be conquered? Answer all these questions will help us to be able to properly read the map. And all this story is only to know that, the forces after pulling down the enemy's flag ,retreat to rest and gather strength again to reach the goal. The aim is to flag down the next summit. Therefore , THE ENGULF is a sign that tell us in advance there is a goal that has not been realized. In next part I try to make some images from the different battlefield. By that I mean look at the history around where price engulfed. Did it engulf into a DP or a key level? Did it engulf into supply/demand. Also, look where the source of the engulf came from, was it coming from a HTF supply/demand level or has it failed yet to reach one? All these things should give you a heads up on a potential FO. For example, if price is engulfing south, but price has yet to come off a significant level of supply, it makes sense to see a FO to help push price to higher levels. Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6700 Lately I had a man-cold, and for a while during that time I'd open the chart and feel I had no idea what I was looking at. I knew I knew the market, but there was still something inside me telling me that I wouldn't be able to read it This wasn't upsetting at all , because I knew full well this malady would pass and I'd be back on top of it again. This can happen to anybody, due to illness, fatigue, fear of failure, fear of success, or any number of other causes. For a student this can be very distressing and debilitating. But it need not be terminal. The problem is not that one's read has gone. The loss of the read is just a manifestation of another problem in life. That's why, when we lose it, we must step away from the charts, and look within ourselves to find the unresolved issues. Once we've faced and fixed them, we can get straight back to work in a better state than if we never had the problem in the first place I remember when I was learning the market, I'd have these EUREKA moments, which were wonderful! I'd think to myself "I've got it! I've got it!" and imagine that now everything I did would be perfect from then on. But it wasn't. I'd still not be right all the time. Soon I'd get another eureka moment, and think I had it again. But no. There are a number of lessons which need to be learned, and each helps. After all these lessons are learned, it still takes time for them all to fit together. Once they do all come together, we don't think "EUREKA". Instead we sigh, and say "I'm ready". IFMYANTE ps. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You "THE ART OF WAR" 19 Oct 2016 09:12 #570 hndrk --> Offline Trader Posts: 22 Thank you received: 36 Hello Salivan, With 'average spread' I mean that if the spread on a pair stays around 1 pip most of the time than I would call the average spread on that pair 1 pip. And with spread I mean the difference between the buy price and the sell price. So if the average spread on a pair is one pip than for a buy limit I would add that to my entry point to ensure a fill. Example: If my level is 1.00 and the average spread is 0.10 then my buy limit is at 1.10. Thank you. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6699 Hi kutumbaba you are very welcome here About Engulf , in fact our weapon in the war between sellers and buyers is ENG as it's the intention of ITs to push price up/down . with out ENG trading will be so hard to find the correct direction of price , so that if we want to know their intention in future we must pay attention to their secret signal that they give to each other in past . in every TF always we have an ENG bcz ENG in term of Order Flow is the only reason for price movement . so Engulf of important S/D is an unrealized goal for big guys .they use ENG to show what they want in future , every ENG has it's own target and in that target big guys again make an other decision to respect the target or break it . after break a target(ENG) then new transaction of orders execute to hold price up/down in future . so generally with out ENG there is no ENG . the question is this : which engulfs are important ? OK , just engulf of important S/D , all the supply are a reaction to a better price as true supply and for demand Vice versa , demand is a reaction to a true demand . our true transaction of orders is FL. FL is the power of nations and price .reading the market in my idea is a science but it's also an art to identify your enemy and the way that they think about you . this war is about money as all the wars are about money .where money printed and where they used it to execute the orders is important for us . if you want to understand this i suggest you to read RTM . about second question : after ENG where should we enter in the direction of ENG ? OK, IMO , we trade in the direction of ENG like the the same as ITs in those places that we have free order flow to push price in the direction of ENG. so that we should read the left orders , but how ? with reading past , always past show you what will happen in future , but again how ? Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6699 Ifmyante quotes  If the signal is given by the market mover (an engulf into a new zone), then price is very unlikely to break the extreme of the zone it just came from. So, if you have the patience to wait at the last remaining set of unfilled orders in the origin, you can be almost certain that that price will be respected.  There is absolute order in the market. Nothing at all there happens by chance. That's why it's so easy to read what's going to happen next. There are rules which are strictly followed; so much so you'd imagine it's all run by algorithms, up to the moment when the signal is decided upon, and straight away thereafter. There is zero chaos in the market. It's elegantly designed; a beauty to behold.  Fakeouts are extremely easy to predict. Most SD traders still look directly left, which is the big shortcoming of Supply/Demand trading. It's further left again we should be looking.  Say price is coming up to a supply. The only way we can be sure that supply will hold price down is if that supply has already visited the extreme set of orders in the flag limit to its left. If the supply fell short of that, we can anticipate a FO to those extreme orders. Extremely simple stuff.  We always look to what S or D are reactions to, rather than just S or D themselves.  Look for tricks being played on approach to a place where a trick was played, and you'll find where price will turn.  If you can look beyond S/D, you'll see that the Flag Limit is the only true place to look for PA for a trade. Trade these levels and you're taking gambling out of your method.  All we can ever hope for is a bounce at these levels, unless we are certain that this level is the deepest possible point of retrace after a previous engulf. Without that, we must watch PA as it develops, both before and during the trade. Set and Forget trades can only be taken once the signal is given and the target is clear.  Being patient is absolutely vital for making giant trades. We must wait for the very best possible places before we enter; the places where you'd expect great PA to react.  If you're around to watch the PA unfold, it's rare your stop should get hit. Price will so very often retrace enough for you to get out without a loss. That's why I wait for the very best price to TT - it tends to keep me in the black.  I'm not even a part time trader now, so I miss nearly every piece of action there is. If I ever open the charts and see a trade opp right in front of me, I take it. However, I usually get between 10R and 25R per trade. If I lose, it's usually no more than the spread and commission. There are between 5 and 20 such confirmed trades available every day.  First of all, we need to understand that time has no place in any read of the market. The only way to be completely sure of where a FL is, is to be there when the break occurs, and mark the highs and lows as they occur. Within a minute they can be obscured by a candle, but we'll know exactly where they are. If we're not there to watch and mark, we must use the full candle as a FL.  If we've had an engulf and are getting in on a RT, we must always be ready for a diamond to occur, especially if price hasn't yet hit MPL of the zone the original bounce was a reaction to. So, if we're not going to be around to watch PA, our stop must be beyond the original FL.  Funny you should say that, as I teach to always and only trade within a flag. Sometimes the flag will already have developed, and sometimes the flag is to be made while you're in the trade. Either way, always trade within a flag.  Attune yourself to what the buggers are doing, and don't let them fool you. Just know they've got orders to fill at a level, watch them fill some on approach (CP), see the momentum, and watch them come back to fill more orders 'til they've had their fill.  This perhaps should be the first thing that anybody ever reads regarding trading: We're always looking for signs of what the big guys are doing at significant areas, and if we don't see what they're doing, there's no trade. So, on approach, if we see the big guys trying to hide their orders in the market, we see compression, and can feel pretty sure of their intentions - to get in as many orders as they can before the turn If we don't see this, we can be pretty sure that it won't just turn immediately, as there usually won't be enough orders against them to fill all the orders they must fill. This is why we wait for an engulf. This shows their intention to reverse price. Then we watch them trying to hide their orders in the market on a retrace, ready to take price to the origin of the move.  When we see decent CP coming into the base of a pole, we are very often safe to touch trade the base. The safest thing to do however is to await the first engulf into the cp zone as confirmation.  Very often a zone will break strongly and price will retrace but fail to retouch it. This is still the FTR - the confirmation of a new trend (do a study of how price reacts and how far it goes after hitting this spot). So an FTR can be first time back, but doesn't need to be.  During holidays, volume in the market is often greatly diminished. This would lead some to imagine that price hardly moves. But. Say someone decided to put a truckload of orders into the market. If there's nobody else in the market to oppose these orders, price can do nothing but shoot away. So remember. Low Volume can = High Volatility.  Until now I have been so unfocused on the charts that my exits have been very sloppy. My trade plan now has a couple of variables, but essentially I'll let price travel back to the other edge of the last PAZ in the TF I'm trading. If it engulfs, I'll exit on a RT or a break of the next LTF FL. If it rejects, I'll let the trade run and await exit PA.  It's all about getting into the mind of the market makers and trading as they do. Nothing special.  Most of my analysis comes in after the trade is entered. Before taking the trade, I do as you said - simple - it's really easy to find pockets of orders which will bounce price, and if they happen to be at great htf levels, even better - there's the highest chance of them giving maximum pips. What I do certainly looks like touch trading - picking tops and bottoms, but what you said belies that. These are not tops and bottoms, but retraces to the best price to re enter. Once I'm in though, I'm never guaranteed massive returns - sure price will bounce where I enter, but I'm never complacent until I've seen the engulf. In fact, I'm never really complacent at all. If PA tells me to get out, I must get out!  Many might misconstrue us as pattern recognition traders - we're not. Certainly while learning we look for recurring patterns in the market. But once we understand them, what becomes most important is WHY the ITs made them. It's paramount to understand that it's not enough for the ITs to simply move price. They must also get massive amounts of orders filled in order to make maximum gains. They must also refrain from giving other ITs false signals, which could ultimately cause chaos for everybody. Think of these things as you study, and you'll be able to get into the mind of the market mover.  Here are just a few targets for price, and the QM level is a big one. Certainly we need to get PA for entry before or once it's hit. If it breaks, then the same level can have the opposite effect on return.  Once price engulfs a level, all that's important is how far it retraces before hitting its target. While the pockets of orders remain in this RT, it remains strong. If price totally compresses (picking up all orders) forward from the tip of the RT, then we will look primarily for the orders at the entrance to said CP.  To the ITs, candle closes don't mean a damned thing, so please don't use them in your own analysis.  A line is not the answer. Certainly, you may draw a line, but you must then go into the LTF to find a DBR/RBD on the right side of the LL/HH swing which covers that line. That RBD/DBR will be your box. You can scalp from each of these, knowing that it may only be a scalp. If you're simply setting a PO, then you must set your stop beyond the FL the HH/LL is a reaction to.  The usable engulf is the one which hasn't hit its target. Every engulf has a very specific target. Apply that statement to your charts and eventually you'll see what I mean.  Being only a sporadic trader (I really couldn't sit and watch the charts all day anymore!), I tend to open the charts from time to time and ask myself what's coming up in the next few minutes for me to take. If I'm lucky, I'll open the charts when we're at an HTF level. If not, I'll gladly take whatever high R M1 or whatever is there for the picking. 30 pips with a 3 pip stop is exactly the same as 150 pips with a 15. If there's nothing decent to take, I shut the charts.  If I were asked where to trade, in one word, I'd say: Stops  I'm way too disorganised to use limit orders! I just open the charts from time to time, and if I see the ITs scaring the retailers into closing good trades at a good level, I enter. I'll take off some of the position at the first target, so if my stop gets taken I can profit overall, then watch PA level by level. If price doesn't get into a big zone quickly, I'll usually get bored and go flat, having made enough to cover my next week's expenses. If I were truly meticulous, I'd treat my exits the same as my entries, and trade up and down all day, but trading is usually way down on my to-do list.  Certainly there's an awful lot to learn here. But if I were to summarise what I think is most important, I'd say look to an engulf into free space that hasn't yet hit the origin (tg). Very often it will retrace deeply before advancing to the origin. Learn to spot these, and you'll be better equipped than most other traders out there.  Price moves from PAZ to PAZ. The clear target for any trade after an engulf is the other end of the PAZ in that TF. If you zoom out to HTFs, you may find the TG is even further, but if not, stick to the TF you're in.  I just want to warn you though that watching candles is an absolute waste of time. It distracts you from reading the story of price. The chart is a page, and a candle is a word. A word in itself has little meaning; it can be taken out of context. Sure, a sentence can be very powerful, as can a group of candles. But to get a real sense of the story, we need to view it all as a whole - be aware of how this paragraph relates to one many chapters back, and get a sense of where the story will lead in the future.  In essence, we know that if price engulfs South, it wants to move down to the last engulf North.  We want to read the story of price, and believe me, price has a story! You'll need to go further left to get your analysis right. Yes, you've marked levels well, but what are those levels a reaction to? Without knowing this, you're just gambling. So, look left, read the story, and be better equipped to predict what'll come next.  Ask yourself "Why did price shoot up from there?" You'll answer "Because someone wanted to buy a lorryload, but there was nobody willing to sell at that price, so price shot up to find sellers." The next question you'll ask yourself is "Will he have left orders to buy again at that price?" The answer is usually "yes". Next question is "will price reverse from there?" The answer is, "Well, it may well bounce form there, but we won't know if it'll reverse until an engulf tells us it's reversed"  Of course, the extremes in one TF can be midrange in another TF, which is why it's vital to manage your adds in the lower TF until they break into HTF trades.  Okay! One giant clue: If something which should have been important got ignored, then it will be given great import on return.  Personally, I love to dissect the HTF zone, in LTF, and look for a DBR or RBD within it, where price had broken out of a box and failed to get back in.  Whipsaw engulfing - a fakeout followed by a quick return breaking the last zone. It's great PA.  An excellent Supply or Demand zone is one where the future has already been written. Having done some study of the markets, we know that once we have an engulf of a zone, price will want to go to the origin. So we look to where the trend change was confirmed - FTR.  You must study the zone which is being reacted to just as much as the reaction itself.  Just consider the manipulation of hope and fear at turning points, and you'll have a very valuable eureka moment.  When you begin to see the symmetry in the market, you're making one of the final steps in reading and predicting it.  High R is High R, and these trades happen with great frequency. I applaud this easy way of making good money. If you're at the MPL of an HTF level, however, think about taking enough at LTF tg1 to cover the HTF stop, and letting the trade run.  A bit of simple advice, to avoid overtrading and impulse trading: Draw up the most important looking zones, and look for trades only there.  We absolutely must have an hard stop, always. But if we don't have an engulf before entry, we don't put it directly above the high or below the low, where all the retail stops lie. Instead, we find a lovely LTF RBD/DBR just beyond, and put it on the other side of that, so that we have the best chance to get out at BE or in big profit from the usual RT.  There's no indication that a demand has been respected until the source above has been engulfed. Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6699 this is the structure of Free Order Flow : price reading article In order to be able to trade the markets, we need to be able to understand why price is where it is, and where it will go to next. The best indicator for all this is Price itself. It holds all the clues you'll ever need to work the market out. We do our trading at levels called Supply and Demand Zones (Video), and we watch Price Action there to give us signs as to the intentions of the big money. Here’s what we look for on the charts: General: HTF. Know where price is coming from and going to, and the PA past and present in all the TFs, from the Monthly down. Specific: At the zones you want to trade, look to Past. study the zone in all TFs, down to M1 ask yourself Where were the decisions made? Clean S/D? Mark these lines. No clean S/D? – compressed zone Did price really shoot away form the zone, or did it cp away? Did the zone itself react at the right place? Look beyond the zone further into the past. See what it reacted to. Was there a better S/D nearby that price wants to visit? This explains many fakeouts. Did price originally react to the RS of a Flag Limit? It can fakeout to true SD of the FL. Present. Approach. How is price returning to the zone? Where’s the nearest flag in the TF you want to trade? This is your tg1 in this TF. Flags in the LTFs? What does PA tell you? Has price tested the last flag on approach? (good sign) Has price compressed into the zone in this TF or LTFs? (good sign) Is there big news on the way? Has there just been big news? Reaction In LTF, does price react violently to the first decision point? Does it quickly engulf the nearest S/D? (good sign) Does price simply CP away? Maybe it wants to go to the next decision point If the first decision point breaks, watch the signs on approach to the next, and, of course, reaction. Chew this over for now. Apply it to your chart history. Apply it to as many failed setups as successful ones. Millions of them if possible! Capture and file them all. This will help make it instinctive and IF's idea about price reading article : Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6699 "Free Order Flow " in order to read the market and understand every price movement in the market we need to investigate the it in terms of true orders that executed in the market .we know that FLs in the only true place in the market that this sets of orders executed in . and also we know that this kind of orders executed after engulf of opposite orders . so what we need again if we can see those orders ? as i told before there are lots of FTRs in one TF but there are few FLs . but every of this FLs also has it's own value in terms of order flow , some are good for a bounce , some will be break with out any bounce and some hold price . how we can understand if those FLs have the orders to hold price or not ? this is the most important question that we should ask every time we look at the market .as we know ITs can not fill all their orders in one place so they have to accumulation the orders to reach their targets . but the places that they are going to start a new trend is FLs. in this case they trade in monthly TF and start accumulation the orders in 1 min TF to their monthly target . so the targets are always important than the entries , bcz if we understand the target we can understand also the whole story for price . but what is FOF and what's it's rule in reading the market ? Free Order Flow is the sets of orders that Clean and apply always in the market by pro moneys , they will create the scenarios by this to shake out retailers and grab some more orders from unsuspected traders . as we know our target and entry are always FLs , so when they engulf a target in fact they are buying /selling in a higher/lower price so in it's scale then are coming back to accumulation of orders and they want to be the only one that sell or buy in the market , but the question is this how we can understand the ITs scenario in the price movement ? this takes thousand of hours and full control in every scale to understand what they are going to do next . as a basic we should understand price reading article that is in the markepedia and also put ITs hat in our head . in order to understand this we should always ask this questions : where price coming from ? a reached target or not ?determine your scale that you want to trade . always look at HTF as it has the major map of price movement and enter in lower TF as they create this map . where is price now ? is it in S/D so it can fake to the extreme orders in to the true S/D . and other parts in price reading article . all my efforts here was to apply reading the market not drawing rectangles , if we want to understand FOF we should understand FLs scales,and targets at first and we should understand big losses for ITs if they don't take out some sets of orders , for example we want to trade daily TF and we find a FL in daily TF to trade it , it's not guarantee that they engulf a daily TF FL for showing us their intention for future , they can engulf a lower scale FL inside that daily FL but don't engulf the daily FL , this is an other way for ITs to showing their intention , that's why i always say try to read the orders . look at the charts below : so FOF has a big relationship with price reading article and targets for pro moneys . they always show their intention inside their targets . how to be able to read FOF in the market : if i want to write a proper way i can say without being able to read the market in terms of FLs and Orders and price reading article we can not read FOF , and it's need massive focus to read it . some clues : basics : 1- understand the full concepts behind RTM stuff ( FTR,FL,QM,CP,CANCAN,CAPS,....) PRO : 1-understand FL in terms of orders not rectangles . 2- understand scale and understand this , that orders are more important than the TFs . 3-understand this they need to left the targets for few pips around their higher scale targets for future . 4-what's CP ? it's a kind of deep RT after engulf . how a CP start to be play in price movment? these whole pieces of puzzel can help you to understand FOF understand price reading article as an Instinctive way . more important than others , without putting thousands hours inside the chart there is no way to understand it as it should be something Instinctive. hope it helps you . regards Salivan Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. A is just the first time back, the key decision has already been made, A is just an FTR unless it becomes the decision to engulf some base or s/r above (as per the last scenario in my last post). I'd be interest to see your take on this and why you would think A might be more important that B. Think of it this way, A is a reaction to B, so which is more important? Where are the orders? where did the imbalance originate? Cheers, Robbie Which was then attended by Rcmacf: rcmacf wrote: The flag limit is the feature which defines the flag. As Robbie stated previously, where the flag goes to beyond the limit is not relevant. (Well, it is relevant in so much as where the areas of S/D are within the flag - as this is where price will react on return, once the flag limit is broken. So, the diagram you've posted above does not show the flag limit, it shows where the flag was (maybe) broken. The full story would be something like I've marked here, where the blue box is the flag limit, defined by the points noted in the green circles ( the FL as the abbreviation). So, what's marked as B is the Decision Point (DP) to break the flag and A is the FTR created after that break. What I see is that the FTR was the price point the ITs used to be aiming for in the past, and would FO to the DP (B) but nowadays, they aim for B, and what was once the FO zone, has become the new target. Now, before going to Sali's findings about FL. Let me put Jurij's post here which may be relevant to the above issue. Jurij wrote: I see that the DP concept causes so much confusion. Sometimes price respects the DP sometimes not. Then the always recurring question, does an eng have to eng the DP too? But think about DP, what is really a DP? This is my view on it: This is what we see This is in terms of orders There's no DP, only order flow and new transactions (FL). Have you not been trading late? It's quiet in here... As I did my homework tracking kinks/FLs, I found one observation and it is to do with 'scale'. And I would like to seek your opinion on this. Is it correct to conclude the following: 1) There are kinks of various size depending on the time scale we look at. Hence a kink that is identified on a daily chart, is more likely to be of larger size than a kink that is found on a 1-min chart. 2) However, the importance of a kink is not a function of its size and the timeframe in which it is found. The importance of a kink depends on what creates it. Hence a tiny 1-min kink, created by the break/engulf of a Daily SR, is more important than another 1-min kink created by the break of a 1-hr SR. 3) Following the same logic as No. 2 above, a 1-min kink that breaks a Daily FL is going to be more important than another 1-min kink that breaks 1-hr FL. So now, when I draw kink/FL, I classify them using the following two parameters: (1) Which timeframe is this FL/kink found? For me the more invisible it is, the more powerful it is. (2) What creates this kink? For me, kink created by breaking a HTF levels (Daily/WK SR) is more important. And of course, a 1-min kink that is found at key locations (LS, Pre-CP) are also more important. I was wondering what is your opinion on the above? Thank you very much. Salivan Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You "THE ART OF WAR" 22 Oct 2017 02:49 #1060 dengaima --> Away Trader Posts: 362 Thank you received: 305 salivan wrote: Hi think about the difference between these two diagrams and you will understand the order flow and why price sometimes turn in the last set of orders and sometimes turn in a lower /higher price. regards Salivan I think the difference between two depends on what's on the left - Has it hit it's target (FL) or has it engulfed the target. If ENGULF, then most likely it would want the very last set of orders before moving on. In the diagram case It can happen with 1. Making HH/HL, luring traders into buying, in expectation of price rallying (in this case can get Trendline/MACD traders and retrace buyers). 2. Setting resistance (Double top, triple top etc.) before the MPL (In this case can get both seller stops and buyers + breakout traders) 3. Making CP (Traders are entering left and right as this can be seen as Triangle Flag forming) 4. QM turning into DM (Trapping Head & Shoulder traders and R/S traders) I am not quite sure about ignored levels, but I think its something along this line: After hitting target and is not retracing enough to hit opposing FL, thus level is ignored - Orders left If Target hit and there is no intention to make a LL then we can expect the FL is getting respected, therefore we wait for local FL to be engulfed and trade back up to previous UFL I hope I atleast made some sense Dengaima Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Let me share my thought on your Gold trade. Start with Daily chart: So, around 8 September 2017, price broke into the compression zone, it cleared two peaks inside the compression but could not break above the 3rd. Now going into 1-min chart to see where these levels were broken: The important engulf should be the one that broke FL-A. Next we zoom into the area above FL-A to see how smaller-scaled FLs interact with each other. Here's where a bit of subjectivity comes in: Would you drew B or C as the FL that held price up? Salivan used B, but remember, neither B or C broke anything significant to the left, so I drew both as I can see price reacting to both. So what happened to price next? Well, FL-C was engulfed and this created FL-D. Price tried to break below B but the first attempt was not successful, it bounced back up towards the MPL of FL-D where it reloaded and then came down to engulf B successfully. It tried to engulf FL-A and again the first attempt was not successful, it bounced up to FL-D again, reloaded, and then came down and finally engulfed A. This tells us that FL-D is very strong since it is the source of the engulf of FL-A. In the meantime, FL-E was created after engulfing B and also the CPAZ inside A. Next I tried to investigate why after engulfing B, price retraced to point [1], was it because of a iQM level in area [3] as pointed out by Salivan? I looked at 10s chart below: So now, imagine we were still on the 8 September, and the chart below is what we were seeing, with all the analysis above, I asked myself the question: Where would I have planned the trade? So while I think it is logical to place SL just above FL-E, I still need to establish a good entry level, and for this, I need to look into 10s chart again to see if there is a clean DP at the MPL of E? What I saw was a small scale QM, so a good level to short would be 1355.343? I apologize if I have uploaded too many charts. AK Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6699 This perhaps should be the first thing that anybody ever reads regarding trading: We're always looking for signs of what the big guys are doing at significant areas, and if we don't see what they're doing, there's no trade So, on approach, if we see the big guys trying to hide their orders in the market, we see compression, and can feel pretty sure of their intentions - to get in as many orders as they can before the turn If we don't see this, we can be pretty sure that it won't just turn immediately, as there usually won't be enough orders against them to fill all the orders they must fill. This is why we wait for an engulf. This shows their intention to reverse price. Then we watch them trying to hide their orders in the market on a retrace, ready to take price to the origin of the move IF This is all there is to the market nothing more ,nothing less . read this golden rule over and over again Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Those retailers who sold in point 2 with the SL above the SUPPLY ZONE when their SL hit it make a buy limit order and the demand increases (LQ increases) but it's not big enough for filling the smart money's short orders. for example in point 2 we have 700k offers (the supply consumed 3 times so that it's weaker than before, less sell order than before) then we need 1000k bid for increasing the price, and after increasing it, the hit SLs turn to buy limit orders and now we have [(1000k-700k=300k)+buy limit orders + break out traders ],by this algorithm the demand increases . In my idea the dogs .they called them Big Boys , Smart Money , IT s . Dogs are loyal to their commitments. And I think all the things that one need in this jungle is loyalty to its commitments. RALLY BASE DROP : Generally We call it supply . it's The resistance against rising prices.it Contains the worst buyers and also some decision points that sellers exceeds buyers . so that if any decision made there that price is too expensive we expect in future the big boys can grab some orders from unsuspecting traders or the worst buyers here again . so that this zone is full of DPs. I think all the market are DP s.in this case Some decisions have been taken to reduce the price . but why they think price is here too expensive ?? Psychologically, people tend to repeat their decisions in life the decisions that altered the course of prices in general are important to us. So that if the price is reduced with these decisions we call this area that the decision have been made in it, supply (RBD).and the same applies to regional demand(DBR).some decision have been taken that price is too cheap so the big boys can grab some orders from the novice traders like me in that area in future again.in this case some decision have been taken to rally the price and support it.so This set of decisions in that area, that the price is cheap cause a DBR for us that we call it DEMAND area . But the quality of development of these areas are important to us. How and in what form they are formed is very important. Do they have a firm decision or indecision has occurred in past ??these are also important . Another issue is approaching the prices to these areas.so that if price approaching to a fresh area as a compression we can expect that area to work again as before. But if price approaching the area Strictly we should wait and use other weapons . I think all the market is fear and greed. Those CPs represents the fear. And high volatility is indicate the greed . so that in greed we should pay more attention to other weapons why the opponent does not fear losing and very assertive in approaching our privacy. our privacy is our castle , where we already have seen fighters failure. If you look into the real world you will see that the losers always fear at The places where they have failed there . So this is a psychological reason. This forest is a mirror of the behavior of its residents. This is what we see in the real world. Castle also been hitting so that it's too weak for the next attack and we call this consumptions of the orders. Weakness or strength of the castle can be determined from something that we call it SUPPLY & DEMAND. I want to say that I see the difference between SUPPLY with RBD and DEMAND with DBR . I will explain the reason, In future. Therefore the more attacking to a castle cause it weaker and in the next raid, it may be rejected by the stronger amount of attackers. This how I read the story . After that we have some other weapons to determine whether a castle resistance against the attacks or not ? Something that called CP. Compression is a kind of fear. But sometimes this is fear that gives courage. My fear is what gives me the courage. Again, these two issues are related to underpin our castle .A new castle usually resistance against the fear of the attackers . Retreat or recess of warriors in the way up toapproaching the castle is a sign that they fear . After reaching the Castle The first warrior who fail ,break the morale of the fighters . On the other hand if the army on the way forward reach to a coward Front ,Of course, it will be faster to defeat it . now what is the difference between SUPPLY and RBD ? Imagine we want to build a fortress. a fortress which contains many castle that Each castle has a flag . in my idea even a strong fortress on a loose ground cannot withstand the attacks .so that I consider supply as a ground as the foundation of the fortress and consider the fortress as RBD. vice versa for DEMAND and DBR too. In the RBD the upper castle in this case the extreme edge of the fortress is SUPPLY area that resistance against the Attackers. The question that must be asked here is that Why this Classifications are important for me ? If attackers can infiltrate a castle after a while they vivify their power then march in the same direction of the seepage to approach another castle on their way . how much to be returning to shore power depends on the strength of the fortress collapsed, that RTM call it as ENGULF . I have another question: Who make this ENGULF ? No one in particular , The only things that make penetration occurs are the fort foundation strength and the strength of the invaders blows. The question is whether the big boy makes an engulf or all attackers make it? Or do engulf pre-made and big boy sees it and then decide for it ? This question also are right and logical . By that I mean look at the history around where price engulfed. Did it engulf into a DP or a key level? Did it engulf into supply/demand. Also, look where the source of the engulf came from, was it coming from a HTF supply/demand level or has it failed yet to reach one? All these things should give you a heads up on a potential FO. For example, if price is engulfing south, but price has yet to come off a significant level of supply, it makes sense to see a FO to help push price to higher levels. The following user(s) said Thank You: greg08088 , salivan Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You "THE ART OF WAR" 13 Oct 2016 17:52 #539 salivan Topic Author --> Offline Master Trader Those who have flown are the ones who have practiced a thousand times falling. Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6700 Lately I had a man-cold, and for a while during that time I'd open the chart and feel I had no idea what I was looking at. I knew I knew the market, but there was still something inside me telling me that I wouldn't be able to read it This wasn't upsetting at all , because I knew full well this malady would pass and I'd be back on top of it again. This can happen to anybody, due to illness, fatigue, fear of failure, fear of success, or any number of other causes. For a student this can be very distressing and debilitating. But it need not be terminal. The problem is not that one's read has gone. The loss of the read is just a manifestation of another problem in life. That's why, when we lose it, we must step away from the charts, and look within ourselves to find the unresolved issues. Once we've faced and fixed them, we can get straight back to work in a better state than if we never had the problem in the first place I remember when I was learning the market, I'd have these EUREKA moments, which were wonderful! I'd think to myself "I've got it! I've got it!" and imagine that now everything I did would be perfect from then on. But it wasn't. I'd still not be right all the time. Soon I'd get another eureka moment, and think I had it again. But no. There are a number of lessons which need to be learned, and each helps. After all these lessons are learned, it still takes time for them all to fit together. Once they do all come together, we don't think "EUREKA". Instead we sigh, and say "I'm ready". IFMYANTE ps. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You "THE ART OF WAR" 19 Oct 2016 09:12 #570 hndrk --> Offline Trader Posts: 22 Thank you received: 36 Hello Salivan, With 'average spread' I mean that if the spread on a pair stays around 1 pip most of the time than I would call the average spread on that pair 1 pip. And with spread I mean the difference between the buy price and the sell price. So if the average spread on a pair is one pip than for a buy limit I would add that to my entry point to ensure a fill. Example: If my level is 1.00 and the average spread is 0.10 then my buy limit is at 1.10. Thank you. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6699 Ifmyante quotes  If the signal is given by the market mover (an engulf into a new zone), then price is very unlikely to break the extreme of the zone it just came from. So, if you have the patience to wait at the last remaining set of unfilled orders in the origin, you can be almost certain that that price will be respected.  There is absolute order in the market. Nothing at all there happens by chance. That's why it's so easy to read what's going to happen next. There are rules which are strictly followed; so much so you'd imagine it's all run by algorithms, up to the moment when the signal is decided upon, and straight away thereafter. There is zero chaos in the market. It's elegantly designed; a beauty to behold.  Fakeouts are extremely easy to predict. Most SD traders still look directly left, which is the big shortcoming of Supply/Demand trading. It's further left again we should be looking.  Say price is coming up to a supply. The only way we can be sure that supply will hold price down is if that supply has already visited the extreme set of orders in the flag limit to its left. If the supply fell short of that, we can anticipate a FO to those extreme orders. Extremely simple stuff.  We always look to what S or D are reactions to, rather than just S or D themselves.  Look for tricks being played on approach to a place where a trick was played, and you'll find where price will turn.  If you can look beyond S/D, you'll see that the Flag Limit is the only true place to look for PA for a trade. Trade these levels and you're taking gambling out of your method.  All we can ever hope for is a bounce at these levels, unless we are certain that this level is the deepest possible point of retrace after a previous engulf. Without that, we must watch PA as it develops, both before and during the trade. Set and Forget trades can only be taken once the signal is given and the target is clear.  Being patient is absolutely vital for making giant trades. We must wait for the very best possible places before we enter; the places where you'd expect great PA to react.  If you're around to watch the PA unfold, it's rare your stop should get hit. Price will so very often retrace enough for you to get out without a loss. That's why I wait for the very best price to TT - it tends to keep me in the black.  I'm not even a part time trader now, so I miss nearly every piece of action there is. If I ever open the charts and see a trade opp right in front of me, I take it. However, I usually get between 10R and 25R per trade. If I lose, it's usually no more than the spread and commission. There are between 5 and 20 such confirmed trades available every day.  First of all, we need to understand that time has no place in any read of the market. The only way to be completely sure of where a FL is, is to be there when the break occurs, and mark the highs and lows as they occur. Within a minute they can be obscured by a candle, but we'll know exactly where they are. If we're not there to watch and mark, we must use the full candle as a FL.  If we've had an engulf and are getting in on a RT, we must always be ready for a diamond to occur, especially if price hasn't yet hit MPL of the zone the original bounce was a reaction to. So, if we're not going to be around to watch PA, our stop must be beyond the original FL.  Funny you should say that, as I teach to always and only trade within a flag. Sometimes the flag will already have developed, and sometimes the flag is to be made while you're in the trade. Either way, always trade within a flag.  Attune yourself to what the buggers are doing, and don't let them fool you. Just know they've got orders to fill at a level, watch them fill some on approach (CP), see the momentum, and watch them come back to fill more orders 'til they've had their fill.  This perhaps should be the first thing that anybody ever reads regarding trading: We're always looking for signs of what the big guys are doing at significant areas, and if we don't see what they're doing, there's no trade. So, on approach, if we see the big guys trying to hide their orders in the market, we see compression, and can feel pretty sure of their intentions - to get in as many orders as they can before the turn If we don't see this, we can be pretty sure that it won't just turn immediately, as there usually won't be enough orders against them to fill all the orders they must fill. This is why we wait for an engulf. This shows their intention to reverse price. Then we watch them trying to hide their orders in the market on a retrace, ready to take price to the origin of the move.  When we see decent CP coming into the base of a pole, we are very often safe to touch trade the base. The safest thing to do however is to await the first engulf into the cp zone as confirmation.  Very often a zone will break strongly and price will retrace but fail to retouch it. This is still the FTR - the confirmation of a new trend (do a study of how price reacts and how far it goes after hitting this spot). So an FTR can be first time back, but doesn't need to be.  During holidays, volume in the market is often greatly diminished. This would lead some to imagine that price hardly moves. But. Say someone decided to put a truckload of orders into the market. If there's nobody else in the market to oppose these orders, price can do nothing but shoot away. So remember. Low Volume can = High Volatility.  Until now I have been so unfocused on the charts that my exits have been very sloppy. My trade plan now has a couple of variables, but essentially I'll let price travel back to the other edge of the last PAZ in the TF I'm trading. If it engulfs, I'll exit on a RT or a break of the next LTF FL. If it rejects, I'll let the trade run and await exit PA.  It's all about getting into the mind of the market makers and trading as they do. Nothing special.  Most of my analysis comes in after the trade is entered. Before taking the trade, I do as you said - simple - it's really easy to find pockets of orders which will bounce price, and if they happen to be at great htf levels, even better - there's the highest chance of them giving maximum pips. What I do certainly looks like touch trading - picking tops and bottoms, but what you said belies that. These are not tops and bottoms, but retraces to the best price to re enter. Once I'm in though, I'm never guaranteed massive returns - sure price will bounce where I enter, but I'm never complacent until I've seen the engulf. In fact, I'm never really complacent at all. If PA tells me to get out, I must get out!  Many might misconstrue us as pattern recognition traders - we're not. Certainly while learning we look for recurring patterns in the market. But once we understand them, what becomes most important is WHY the ITs made them. It's paramount to understand that it's not enough for the ITs to simply move price. They must also get massive amounts of orders filled in order to make maximum gains. They must also refrain from giving other ITs false signals, which could ultimately cause chaos for everybody. Think of these things as you study, and you'll be able to get into the mind of the market mover.  Here are just a few targets for price, and the QM level is a big one. Certainly we need to get PA for entry before or once it's hit. If it breaks, then the same level can have the opposite effect on return.  Once price engulfs a level, all that's important is how far it retraces before hitting its target. While the pockets of orders remain in this RT, it remains strong. If price totally compresses (picking up all orders) forward from the tip of the RT, then we will look primarily for the orders at the entrance to said CP.  To the ITs, candle closes don't mean a damned thing, so please don't use them in your own analysis.  A line is not the answer. Certainly, you may draw a line, but you must then go into the LTF to find a DBR/RBD on the right side of the LL/HH swing which covers that line. That RBD/DBR will be your box. You can scalp from each of these, knowing that it may only be a scalp. If you're simply setting a PO, then you must set your stop beyond the FL the HH/LL is a reaction to.  The usable engulf is the one which hasn't hit its target. Every engulf has a very specific target. Apply that statement to your charts and eventually you'll see what I mean.  Being only a sporadic trader (I really couldn't sit and watch the charts all day anymore!), I tend to open the charts from time to time and ask myself what's coming up in the next few minutes for me to take. If I'm lucky, I'll open the charts when we're at an HTF level. If not, I'll gladly take whatever high R M1 or whatever is there for the picking. 30 pips with a 3 pip stop is exactly the same as 150 pips with a 15. If there's nothing decent to take, I shut the charts.  If I were asked where to trade, in one word, I'd say: Stops  I'm way too disorganised to use limit orders! I just open the charts from time to time, and if I see the ITs scaring the retailers into closing good trades at a good level, I enter. I'll take off some of the position at the first target, so if my stop gets taken I can profit overall, then watch PA level by level. If price doesn't get into a big zone quickly, I'll usually get bored and go flat, having made enough to cover my next week's expenses. If I were truly meticulous, I'd treat my exits the same as my entries, and trade up and down all day, but trading is usually way down on my to-do list.  Certainly there's an awful lot to learn here. But if I were to summarise what I think is most important, I'd say look to an engulf into free space that hasn't yet hit the origin (tg). Very often it will retrace deeply before advancing to the origin. Learn to spot these, and you'll be better equipped than most other traders out there.  Price moves from PAZ to PAZ. The clear target for any trade after an engulf is the other end of the PAZ in that TF. If you zoom out to HTFs, you may find the TG is even further, but if not, stick to the TF you're in.  I just want to warn you though that watching candles is an absolute waste of time. It distracts you from reading the story of price. The chart is a page, and a candle is a word. A word in itself has little meaning; it can be taken out of context. Sure, a sentence can be very powerful, as can a group of candles. But to get a real sense of the story, we need to view it all as a whole - be aware of how this paragraph relates to one many chapters back, and get a sense of where the story will lead in the future.  In essence, we know that if price engulfs South, it wants to move down to the last engulf North.  We want to read the story of price, and believe me, price has a story! You'll need to go further left to get your analysis right. Yes, you've marked levels well, but what are those levels a reaction to? Without knowing this, you're just gambling. So, look left, read the story, and be better equipped to predict what'll come next.  Ask yourself "Why did price shoot up from there?" You'll answer "Because someone wanted to buy a lorryload, but there was nobody willing to sell at that price, so price shot up to find sellers." The next question you'll ask yourself is "Will he have left orders to buy again at that price?" The answer is usually "yes". Next question is "will price reverse from there?" The answer is, "Well, it may well bounce form there, but we won't know if it'll reverse until an engulf tells us it's reversed"  Of course, the extremes in one TF can be midrange in another TF, which is why it's vital to manage your adds in the lower TF until they break into HTF trades.  Okay! One giant clue: If something which should have been important got ignored, then it will be given great import on return.  Personally, I love to dissect the HTF zone, in LTF, and look for a DBR or RBD within it, where price had broken out of a box and failed to get back in.  Whipsaw engulfing - a fakeout followed by a quick return breaking the last zone. It's great PA.  An excellent Supply or Demand zone is one where the future has already been written. Having done some study of the markets, we know that once we have an engulf of a zone, price will want to go to the origin. So we look to where the trend change was confirmed - FTR.  You must study the zone which is being reacted to just as much as the reaction itself.  Just consider the manipulation of hope and fear at turning points, and you'll have a very valuable eureka moment.  When you begin to see the symmetry in the market, you're making one of the final steps in reading and predicting it.  High R is High R, and these trades happen with great frequency. I applaud this easy way of making good money. If you're at the MPL of an HTF level, however, think about taking enough at LTF tg1 to cover the HTF stop, and letting the trade run.  A bit of simple advice, to avoid overtrading and impulse trading: Draw up the most important looking zones, and look for trades only there.  We absolutely must have an hard stop, always. But if we don't have an engulf before entry, we don't put it directly above the high or below the low, where all the retail stops lie. Instead, we find a lovely LTF RBD/DBR just beyond, and put it on the other side of that, so that we have the best chance to get out at BE or in big profit from the usual RT.  There's no indication that a demand has been respected until the source above has been engulfed. The following user(s) said Thank You: cuimingzhao Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You "THE ART OF WAR" 27 Dec 2016 19:14 #824 salivan Topic Author --> Offline Master Trader Those who have flown are the ones who have practiced a thousand times falling. Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6699 this is the structure of Free Order Flow : price reading article In order to be able to trade the markets, we need to be able to understand why price is where it is, and where it will go to next. The best indicator for all this is Price itself. It holds all the clues you'll ever need to work the market out. We do our trading at levels called Supply and Demand Zones (Video), and we watch Price Action there to give us signs as to the intentions of the big money. Here’s what we look for on the charts: General: HTF. Know where price is coming from and going to, and the PA past and present in all the TFs, from the Monthly down. Specific: At the zones you want to trade, look to Past. study the zone in all TFs, down to M1 ask yourself Where were the decisions made? Clean S/D? Mark these lines. No clean S/D? – compressed zone Did price really shoot away form the zone, or did it cp away? Did the zone itself react at the right place? Look beyond the zone further into the past. See what it reacted to. Was there a better S/D nearby that price wants to visit? This explains many fakeouts. Did price originally react to the RS of a Flag Limit? It can fakeout to true SD of the FL. Present. Approach. How is price returning to the zone? Where’s the nearest flag in the TF you want to trade? This is your tg1 in this TF. Flags in the LTFs? What does PA tell you? Has price tested the last flag on approach? (good sign) Has price compressed into the zone in this TF or LTFs? (good sign) Is there big news on the way? Has there just been big news? Reaction In LTF, does price react violently to the first decision point? Does it quickly engulf the nearest S/D? (good sign) Does price simply CP away? Maybe it wants to go to the next decision point If the first decision point breaks, watch the signs on approach to the next, and, of course, reaction. Chew this over for now. Apply it to your chart history. Apply it to as many failed setups as successful ones. Millions of them if possible! Capture and file them all. This will help make it instinctive and IF's idea about price reading article : Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6699 "Free Order Flow " in order to read the market and understand every price movement in the market we need to investigate the it in terms of true orders that executed in the market .we know that FLs in the only true place in the market that this sets of orders executed in . and also we know that this kind of orders executed after engulf of opposite orders . so what we need again if we can see those orders ? as i told before there are lots of FTRs in one TF but there are few FLs . but every of this FLs also has it's own value in terms of order flow , some are good for a bounce , some will be break with out any bounce and some hold price . how we can understand if those FLs have the orders to hold price or not ? this is the most important question that we should ask every time we look at the market .as we know ITs can not fill all their orders in one place so they have to accumulation the orders to reach their targets . but the places that they are going to start a new trend is FLs. in this case they trade in monthly TF and start accumulation the orders in 1 min TF to their monthly target . so the targets are always important than the entries , bcz if we understand the target we can understand also the whole story for price . but what is FOF and what's it's rule in reading the market ? Free Order Flow is the sets of orders that Clean and apply always in the market by pro moneys , they will create the scenarios by this to shake out retailers and grab some more orders from unsuspected traders . as we know our target and entry are always FLs , so when they engulf a target in fact they are buying /selling in a higher/lower price so in it's scale then are coming back to accumulation of orders and they want to be the only one that sell or buy in the market , but the question is this how we can understand the ITs scenario in the price movement ? this takes thousand of hours and full control in every scale to understand what they are going to do next . as a basic we should understand price reading article that is in the markepedia and also put ITs hat in our head . in order to understand this we should always ask this questions : where price coming from ? a reached target or not ?determine your scale that you want to trade . always look at HTF as it has the major map of price movement and enter in lower TF as they create this map . where is price now ? is it in S/D so it can fake to the extreme orders in to the true S/D . and other parts in price reading article . all my efforts here was to apply reading the market not drawing rectangles , if we want to understand FOF we should understand FLs scales,and targets at first and we should understand big losses for ITs if they don't take out some sets of orders , for example we want to trade daily TF and we find a FL in daily TF to trade it , it's not guarantee that they engulf a daily TF FL for showing us their intention for future , they can engulf a lower scale FL inside that daily FL but don't engulf the daily FL , this is an other way for ITs to showing their intention , that's why i always say try to read the orders . look at the charts below : so FOF has a big relationship with price reading article and targets for pro moneys . they always show their intention inside their targets . how to be able to read FOF in the market : if i want to write a proper way i can say without being able to read the market in terms of FLs and Orders and price reading article we can not read FOF , and it's need massive focus to read it . some clues : basics : 1- understand the full concepts behind RTM stuff ( FTR,FL,QM,CP,CANCAN,CAPS,....) PRO : 1-understand FL in terms of orders not rectangles . 2- understand scale and understand this , that orders are more important than the TFs . 3-understand this they need to left the targets for few pips around their higher scale targets for future . 4-what's CP ? it's a kind of deep RT after engulf . how a CP start to be play in price movment? these whole pieces of puzzel can help you to understand FOF understand price reading article as an Instinctive way . more important than others , without putting thousands hours inside the chart there is no way to understand it as it should be something Instinctive. hope it helps you . regards Salivan Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Is it correct to conclude the following: 1) There are kinks of various size depending on the time scale we look at. Hence a kink that is identified on a daily chart, is more likely to be of larger size than a kink that is found on a 1-min chart. 2) However, the importance of a kink is not a function of its size and the timeframe in which it is found. The importance of a kink depends on what creates it. Hence a tiny 1-min kink, created by the break/engulf of a Daily SR, is more important than another 1-min kink created by the break of a 1-hr SR. 3) Following the same logic as No. 2 above, a 1-min kink that breaks a Daily FL is going to be more important than another 1-min kink that breaks 1-hr FL. So now, when I draw kink/FL, I classify them using the following two parameters: (1) Which timeframe is this FL/kink found? For me the more invisible it is, the more powerful it is. (2) What creates this kink? For me, kink created by breaking a HTF levels (Daily/WK SR) is more important. And of course, a 1-min kink that is found at key locations (LS, Pre-CP) are also more important. I was wondering what is your opinion on the above? Thank you very much. Salivan Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You "THE ART OF WAR" 22 Oct 2017 02:49 #1060 dengaima --> Away Trader Posts: 362 Thank you received: 305 salivan wrote: Hi think about the difference between these two diagrams and you will understand the order flow and why price sometimes turn in the last set of orders and sometimes turn in a lower /higher price. regards Salivan I think the difference between two depends on what's on the left - Has it hit it's target (FL) or has it engulfed the target. If ENGULF, then most likely it would want the very last set of orders before moving on. In the diagram case It can happen with 1. Making HH/HL, luring traders into buying, in expectation of price rallying (in this case can get Trendline/MACD traders and retrace buyers). 2. Setting resistance (Double top, triple top etc.) before the MPL (In this case can get both seller stops and buyers + breakout traders) 3. Making CP (Traders are entering left and right as this can be seen as Triangle Flag forming) 4. QM turning into DM (Trapping Head & Shoulder traders and R/S traders) I am not quite sure about ignored levels, but I think its something along this line: After hitting target and is not retracing enough to hit opposing FL, thus level is ignored - Orders left If Target hit and there is no intention to make a LL then we can expect the FL is getting respected, therefore we wait for local FL to be engulfed and trade back up to previous UFL I hope I atleast made some sense Dengaima Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6699 This perhaps should be the first thing that anybody ever reads regarding trading: We're always looking for signs of what the big guys are doing at significant areas, and if we don't see what they're doing, there's no trade So, on approach, if we see the big guys trying to hide their orders in the market, we see compression, and can feel pretty sure of their intentions - to get in as many orders as they can before the turn If we don't see this, we can be pretty sure that it won't just turn immediately, as there usually won't be enough orders against them to fill all the orders they must fill. This is why we wait for an engulf. This shows their intention to reverse price. Then we watch them trying to hide their orders in the market on a retrace, ready to take price to the origin of the move IF This is all there is to the market nothing more ,nothing less . read this golden rule over and over again Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Posts: 1489 Thank you received: 6699 hi my friend , welcome to your committee nice questions from you here . yes you right there are some question that answering to them needs knowing the Philosophy of the peoples behind the chart . really they can not hide their thought if we look in to the eyes. in the following chart i wrote some notes for you and it's better to read a quote from MASTER Pedini. what I will do when I see an engulf is ask myself "does this engulf make sense?" By that I mean look at the history around where price engulfed. Did it engulf into a DP or a key level? Did it engulf into supply/demand. Also, look where the source of the engulf came from, was it coming from a HTF supply/demand level or has it failed yet to reach one? All these things should give you a heads up on a potential FO. For example, if price is engulfing south, but price has yet to come off a significant level of supply, it makes sense to see a FO to help push price to higher levels.
